question.text: Which type of recurring reporting-system failure has FIU-IND repeatedly cited when acting against reporting entities under the PMLA?

answer.text: Failure to detect, analyse and file required Suspicious Transaction Reports within prescribed timelines
Failure to achieve high investment returns for clients
Failure to open a minimum number of new client accounts per quarter
Failure to advertise AML policies on the company website

explanation.text: The Logic: FIU-IND actions against reporting entities have repeatedly involved failures in the suspicious transaction reporting system — specifically failure to detect, analyse and file required STRs within prescribed timelines, and not implementing systems to identify and report suspicious transactions. Separate categories of FIU-IND/SEBI action also cover registration non-compliance and general cash/suspicious report obligations. The Trap: Investment returns and new-account opening are business performance metrics, not AML compliance requirements. Website advertising of AML policies is not a specific FIU-IND obligation. Not every FIU-IND action is a CTR filing case — many involve STR detection and analysis failures. Note: Reporting-entity obligations and the FIU-IND cases discussed (including the failure to handle/report STRs and failure to detect/report suspicious transactions) are covered on pages 31, 109-110, 120 and 121 of the NISM Series XXIV AML and CFT Provisions in Securities Markets Certification Examination Workbook (November 2025).
